# Professionals Studio stability plan

This plan follows the engineering audit and stress testing requested on 7 September 2026. It separates fixes made in this engineering loop from work that still needs implementation or verification. Creative Studio remains the owner of brand rules and approved campaign content.

## Latest continuation

The autonomous adaptation pass is complete for the normal Studio workflow. Preview and export now consume the same ratio family master. A prepared master is no longer discarded because a placement is larger than the source. Unsafe button and field combinations are resolved from approved brand colours before rendering. When a required logo cannot sit safely on the requested Teal field, the renderer keeps the layout and copy but chooses the first approved neutral field itself. The English and German interfaces both explain the automatic correction.

Two live five placement checks were completed. A photo based Negative space portrait set built all 20 requested files, including 4:5 and 9:16 outputs that had previously been withheld. A typography only set requested on Teal also built all 20 files after the logo surface was resolved automatically to Sand. No user repair step was required in either build.

The [export clarity follow up](./engineering-followup-2026-09-07.md) records the next implementation pass. Internal Studio steps have been removed from customer landing pages. Landing page and email drafts are now optional selections in the Assets step, with accurate counts and saved choices. Built, draft and withheld results are clearer. Actual download delivery in the in app browser still needs confirmation; the follow up does not replace the earlier archive evidence below.

The landing content cleanup in Phase 1 is implemented. The optional output item in Phase 2 is implemented for additions to an image export plan; a separate document only route remains open. Partial result messaging is improved, but the immutable result manifest remains open. Continue with download delivery confirmation, required content and protected subject areas before extending the interface further.

They do not establish behaviour in every browser or email client. |

The production workflow must continue to be tested through the adapter as well as at the renderer boundary. Photo subject protection still needs human review. |

The photo route included the previously failing 4:5 and 9:16 families. The Teal typography route resolved its required logo surface automatically. | The existing archive audit remains the evidence for ZIP integrity. This pass did not repeat a physical browser download or test live paid image extension. |
| Responsive pages | Six product pages passed at narrow, tablet and desktop widths, for 18 checks. No horizontal overflow, broken visible images or wrong rendered typeface remained. | These are route loading checks. Deep modal keyboard flows and every intermediate mobile workflow state still need coverage. |

| Language and persistence | Language switching now survives blocked storage. Database operations have deadlines and cleanup. A reproduced write after a reported timeout was fixed. | Complete translation coverage and a shared persistence schema remain open. |
| Reference templates | The social, landing page and email references no longer contain consumer membership claims, fictitious Professionals tiers or Plus symbols. | These are references. Campaign proof, destinations and production approval must still be supplied. |
| Fonts and email | Font embedding was integrated for generated landing and email HTML. Generated email now visibly states that it is a draft and identifies missing legal destinations. | Rendering in actual sending systems and email clients has not been tested. Live paid API generation and its failure modes have not been validated by this local loop. |

## Phase 1: Make production readiness explicit

| Priority | Confirmed issue and evidence | Next change | Acceptance test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First | Generated landing pages still insert the internal Studio workflow, including “In vier Schritten zur Kampagne”, regardless of the audience brief. See `buildLandingPage` in [story-builder.js](../src/story-builder.js). | Keep the campaign headline, image, supplied proof and intended action. Remove internal Studio instructions from customer outputs. Add a section only when the brief supplies appropriate approved content. | Build campaigns for an agency, property manager and developer. Each export must contain its own supplied message and no production instructions presented as customer benefits. Empty sections must not acquire invented content. |
| First | Technical renderability does not establish whether product claims, required copy or legal content are approved. Some small layouts can reduce secondary copy. See the copy adaptation and export decisions in [ad-engine.js](../src/ad-engine.js) and [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Distinguish mandatory content from optional copy before composition. Require sources for product and performance claims. Never silently remove mandatory words or legal lines. Show the exact missing requirement and preserve a draft preview when production export is unavailable. | Use a long mandatory disclaimer, an unsupported numerical claim, an empty headline and a valid short campaign. The first three must have explicit unresolved outcomes. No placement may export after silently dropping required content. |
| First | Saliency and focal positioning are useful composition signals, but they cannot prove that a face, hand or meaningful object is fully protected. See [size-adapter.js](../src/size-adapter.js) and [ad-engine.js](../src/ad-engine.js). | Let the user confirm a protected subject area on the source image. Carry that area through each crop and contained image treatment. Ask for confirmation again when the source changes. | Test portraits near each edge, two people, hands holding a document and a manual focal adjustment. Every export must preserve the confirmed subject area or explain which placement needs another source or design. |
| First | Draft email exports have no confirmed legal destinations by default. `emailReadiness` in [story-builder.js](../src/story-builder.js) now identifies this and keeps the draft label. | Add controlled fields for approved destination and legal links. Check the actual sending system with the approved font and image treatment before providing a production email status. | Missing, relative and invalid destinations remain draft. Test real delivered messages in the clients used by the team. Record font, image, button and footer results; do not infer success from the browser preview. |

## Phase 2: Make the workflow predictable

| Priority | Confirmed issue and evidence | Next change | Acceptance test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next | Some dynamically generated Studio labels and notices remain English after switching language. The language change handler currently covers only part of the workflow. See [language.js](../src/language.js) and [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Move interface strings into one complete English and German catalogue. Keep German customer copy distinct from interface language. Translate empty states, errors, progress, history and accessible labels as well as headings. | Complete the workflow in both languages, switch during each step, reopen history and reload with blocked storage. No interface section may unexpectedly retain the other language. |
| Next | Modal handling provides a close button, backdrop dismissal and Escape, but does not consistently define dialog semantics or manage focus. See `openModal` and `wireModal` in [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Use one shared dialog behaviour with a name, initial focus, contained keyboard focus and return to the opening control. Ensure all controls remain reachable at narrow widths. | Open every modal using only a keyboard. Tab must stay inside it, Escape must close only the active dialog, and focus must return to the opener. Repeat at a narrow viewport and enlarged text size. |
| Next | A build may deliver only part of a requested set. Rendering, history, approval and downloads must describe the same result. See [studio-facts.js](../src/studio-facts.js), `renderSet` and the archive creation in [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Use one immutable result manifest for planned, built, withheld and failed outputs. Give partial sets a visible partial status and list every omitted file with its reason. Apply the same status in history and the downloaded manifest. | Request a mixed set containing valid, impossible and unsupported placements. Counts must reconcile, withheld files must be absent from the ZIP, and a partial set must never be described as complete. |
| Next | Landing and email documents are produced together by `buildCampaignPages`, even when the requested work is only an image asset. See [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Make landing page and email output explicit choices in the export plan. Include only requested deliverables in progress, counts and the archive. | Build a social only set, a landing only set and a mixed set. Each archive must contain exactly the requested types, without hidden extra documents. |
| Next | Language, campaign history, image records and build records use separate persistence paths. Error handling is improved, but there is no unified schema migration and recovery contract. See [image-library.js](../src/image-library.js), [build-records.js](../src/build-records.js) and history handling in [concept-studio.html](../src/concept-studio.html). | Define versioned record schemas, validate restored rows and provide a recoverable error when data cannot be read. Preserve the last good saved state when a new write fails. Keep credentials out of durable browser records. | Exercise malformed JSON, valid JSON of the wrong shape, an older schema, a quota error and two open tabs. Previously saved work must remain recoverable; the interface must explain which new changes were not saved. |

## Phase 3: Make releases repeatable

| Priority | Confirmed issue and evidence | Next change | Acceptance test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Then | An old cached page could reappear when navigating from the dashboard, while a fresh query showed the new page. The local server now has a development cache fix. | Define one release version for the page, modules, styles and published brand data. Use a consistent cache policy for deployment and verify that a page cannot mix files from different releases. | Open an old tab, release an update, then reload and navigate from the dashboard. Both paths must load a consistent current release without manually editing the URL. |
| Then | The local project has no Git repository or automated release pipeline configured. Regression commands and browser checks currently depend on a manual run. | Establish the source repository and a repeatable validation command. Run unit regressions, source and mirror validation, the renderer matrix, responsive routes and archive integrity checks before publishing. Keep visual review evidence for changed design families. | A deliberately broken font, missing image, unsafe text position or stale published token file must fail the release check. A successful release must include the tested version and its report. |
| Then | Brand facts and implementation are duplicated in places, and [brief.md](./brief.md) and [plan.md](./plan.md) still describe an earlier, much smaller product. An unused [professionals-studio.js](../src/professionals-studio.js) also remains. | Update the product contract to match the accepted workflow. Consolidate shared rules and retire unused paths once their callers have been checked. Keep canonical brand values and generated downloads synchronized. | A new contributor must be able to identify the active routes, source of truth, export rules and test command without following obsolete workflow instructions. A token change must be reflected everywhere through the publication process. |
| Then | External generation and extension involve long requests, credentials, cancellation and source changes. Local simulations do not prove the live integration. | Add controlled integration tests for authorization failure, rate limiting, slow responses, cancellation and late results. Preserve the currently selected image when a stale request returns. | A delayed result must never overwrite a newer image. Failed or cancelled requests must stop their progress state, retain the last usable design and provide a specific recovery action. Record which live cases were actually exercised. |

## Release decision

Treat an asset as technically ready only when its requested format, image quality, protected areas, mandatory content, fonts and output file checks are complete. Technical readiness does not establish a claim, licence or campaign approval.

Use the same status in the preview, result summary, history and archive. Where a check remains pending, say what is missing and which file or placement it affects. Keep the next engineering loop focused on the first unresolved priority above rather than adding more controls to the workflow.
